correctness.rationale: Exact algebra: all intensity cross-terms except the leading diagonal term have degree at most 4d-2, and the leading diagonal term is an even polynomial, so the coefficient at degree 4d-1 is zero. Generalized Vandermonde evaluation is invertible precisely under the stated sufficient condition. The two quadratic fiber reflections act on the rational quotient and compose to translation by 2i, forcing it to be constant. Degree-one zero-sum failure follows because the Hermitian form-to-intensity map is a real-linear isomorphism, its kernel cannot contain a nonzero semidefinite form and every nonzero indefinite 2-by-2 Hermitian form splits into a difference of rank-one forms. The fixed-node stability statement follows by compactness of the rank-two Frobenius unit sphere. Standalone exact checker verified 22 exact assertions in d=1..4; these finite checks do not prove the universal result.

originality.rationale: The main directly inspected 2019 polynomial-intensity algorithm uses (2d+1)^2 measurements on many radii and angles, rather than 4d arbitrary distinct positive nodes of a single parabola. The 2023 Liehr theorem has infinite-dimensional holomorphic functions on unions of parallel lines; the 2024 Chalendar--Partington results concern two lines and circles, not the parabolic all-node finite theorem. Accessible existing findings on two rays, concentric circles and isolated polynomial designs do not imply arbitrary-node parabolic sampling. Public semantic-search matches address root hulls, graph reach and Fourier phase minima, rather than this exact implication. A different curve-reflection theorem may cover the statement and would overturn this originality judgment. A 2017 author presentation confirms the distinct two-concentric-circle 4d result and does not establish arbitrary parabolic node configurations.

value.rationale: Natural practical problem: exact phaseless interpolation of an arbitrary complex degree-d polynomial when measuring only on one connected, explicitly parametrized nonlinear sensor path. The result replaces a multi-ring quadratic-size polynomial interpolation construction with 4d deterministic sites and, unusually, works for every collection of distinct positive nodes even in arbitrarily short arcs. It identifies a genuine algebraic boundary (zero node sum for degree one), gives a closed interpolation matrix, and proves fixed-design stability. This is an object-wide all-degree result, not a routine numerical example or a pretabulated invariant; broader optimality and robust design remain open.
